To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cGMP, in addition to cAMP, is involved in the regulation of ovarian ecdysteroids in a fly.
cGMP is a strong negative regulator of ovarian steroidogenesis, which is mediated by a cGMP-dependent protein kinase.
cGMP, besides its role as an antagonist of cAMP, is a potent inhibitor of ovarian steroidogenesis in the female blow fly Phormia regia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new mechanism of control of ovarian steroid production in insects.
the discovery of a novel mechanism of control of ovarian ecdysteroids in insects.
the identification and functional characterization of the cyclic nucleotide signaling pathways in the control of steroidogenesis in the blowfly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in blowflies, cAMP is the main positive regulator, and cGMP and NO the main negative regulators, of the steroidogenic pathway in ovary.

cGMP and cAMP, which both act as antagonistic second messengers in the regulation of ovarian steroidogenesis in the female blowflies, are probably the most important intracellular messengers in this process.
cGMP is a key regulator of ovarian steroidogenesis, acting antagonistically to cAMP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cGMP, through the control of ovarian ecdysteroids, is able to influence the onset of vitellogenin synthesis in the fat body and, consequently, the onset of vitellin production by the ovary.
the cyclic nucleotide balance in the blowfly ovary is crucial for the control of ovarian steroidogenic activity.
cGMP and NO are involved in a negative control of steroidogenesis, which may be mediated by a protein kinase G.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of insect ovarian ecdysteroids by the cGMP signaling pathway has been shown for the first time.
cGMP is a negative regulator of ovarian steroidogenesis in insects, a role that is not restricted to the ovary but may also occur in other tissues, such as the fat body.
the cAMP/cGMP balance is a key factor in the regulation of insect steroidogenesis.
